note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Is a control valve bypassed, or oversized for its line?

evidence.text: valve FV-A reads "FV-A Fictional flow control valve" at U-A
hand valve HV-A reads "HV-A Fictional bypass valve" at U-A

where: historian or DCS trend for FV-A (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)

questions.decision_rule: Resize or trim when the valve normally runs well under half open or the bypass is cracked open.

typical_benefit.wording: "Many control valves normally operate at less than 50% open... a high degree of nonlinearity and thus inconsistent control performance." No % stated.
source_titles: S13: Improving Pumping System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 2nd ed. (DOE + Hydraulic Institute; DOE/GO-102006-2079)
